precepts.text: Sem and Seth were in great honour among men, and so was Adam above every living thing in the creation. Adam had his righteous child, Seth, and Noah had his righteous child, Shem, and out of Shem's line came us.
precepts.point: And Noah was five hundred years old: and Noah begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
Genesis 5 keeps saying each father “begat sons and daughters,” yet it names specific sons, because those particular children were significant: they birthed prophets. Among the other sons and daughters there was wickedness. That is why Noah is named and found perfect: he had siblings, but he was the righteous one out of all the sons of God of his time dealing with the daughters of men.

Sirach names the righteous line: “Sem and Seth were in great honour among men, and so was Adam above every living thing in creation.” Adam had his righteous child, Seth, born “in his own likeness, after his image,” and Noah had his righteous child, Shem: “Noah begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.”

And out of Shem's line came us. The line God honoured runs from Adam through Seth to Noah and on through Shem to Israel.

precepts.text: Simon the high priest, son of Onias, repaired the house again and fortified the temple. These renowned men earned their names by building back and walking in integrity. Go through Sirach 44 to 50 again on your own; the class only jumped through them.
precepts.point: Of the twelve prophets, let their memorial be blessed, for they comforted Jacob and delivered them by assured hope. Zerubbabel was as a signet on the right hand. Nehemiah, whose renown is great, raised up the fallen walls and re-established the laws so nobody would have the people shopping on the Sabbath. Joseph was a governor of his brethren and a stay of the people.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
After Josias, the twelve prophets, Zorobabel, Neemias and Joseph, Sirach carries the line of renowned men on to the priesthood: “Simon the high priest, the son of Onias, who in his life repaired the house again, and in his days fortified the temple”. Simon repaired the house again. Like Neemias, “who raised up for us the walls that were fallen, and set up the gates and the bars, and raised up our ruins again”, his name is tied to building back what was broken down.

That is how these renowned men earned their names. It was about building back, walking in integrity, moving right. Josias “behaved himself uprightly in the conversion of the people”, not using his position to take advantage of the people or handling the word of God deceitfully. Neemias raised the walls and established the laws again, so nobody would come in trying to get our people to shop on the Sabbath. Simon repaired and fortified the house of God.

So it is with us: “in the time of the ungodly he established the worship of God.” In the midst of all this debauchery we are to establish the worship of God, with no hypocrisy, no covetousness and no murmuring, so that the people see us and say these are those guys we heard about that are going to come back on the earth. That is how you become the famous man.

The class only jumped through these chapters for time’s sake. Go through Sirach 44 to 50 again on your own, because there is a lot more in them.

precepts.text: All except David, Ezekias, and Josias were defective and forsook the law; therefore their power was given unto others, and their glory to a strange nation.
precepts.point: Israel once had mighty kings who ruled over countries beyond the river, and tribute and custom were paid unto them. The kings failed when they forsook the law, and their power was given to a strange nation; that is why the kings of the scriptures are not known as black kings today. When the King of kings returns He restores the crowns, and He sets crowns on the heads of the great multitude on mount Sion.

note.label: Genesis 35: Bethel and the Twelve Sons of Israel

precepts.why:
“All, except David and Ezekias and Josias, were defective: for they forsook the law of the most High, even the kings of Juda failed. Therefore he gave their power unto others, and their glory to a strange nation.”

Kings came out of Jacob's loins as promised, and the kings failed when they forsook the law. Their power was given unto others and their glory to a strange nation; that is why the kings of the scriptures are not known as black kings today. When the King of kings returns He restores the crowns.

precepts.text: No man was born like unto Joseph; put on the spirit of the forefathers.
precepts.point: Neither was there a man born like unto Joseph, a governor of his brethren, a stay of the people, whose bones were regarded of the Lord. To grow in spirit and be like him, put on the spirit of the forefathers.

note.label: Genesis 47: Goshen, the Famine, and the Fifth Part

precepts.why:
“Neither was there a young man born like Joseph, a governor of his brethren, a stay of the people, whose bones were regarded of the Lord.” No man was born like unto Joseph. He governed his brethren, he was the stay of the people through the famine, and his bones were regarded of the Lord, the bones he gave commandment about as his father gave commandment about his own burial here.

To grow in spirit and be like him, put on the spirit of the forefathers.

precepts.point: Yet Jehu takes no heed to walk in the law of the Most High with all his heart, showing that a man may do great things and still turn away and stay in sin.

note.label: 2 Kings 10: Jehu Destroys Baal and Falls Short of the Law

precepts.why:
“All, except David and Ezekias and Josias, were defective: for they forsook the law of the most High, even the kings of Juda failed.”

Jehu is counted among the defective. He destroyed Baal out of Israel, and the Most High commended him for doing to the house of Ahab all that was in his heart. Yet he departed not from the golden calves in Beth-el and in Dan, and “took no heed to walk in the law of the Lord God of Israel with all his heart.”

Only David, Hezekiah and Josiah stand apart. A man may do great things and still turn away and stay in sin.

precepts.point: When the kingdom was confirmed, he slew the servants who had killed his father, but did not slay their children, according to the law of Moses that every man is put to death for his own sin.

note.label: 2 Kings 14: Amaziah, the Imperfect Heart, and Jeroboam II

precepts.why:
“All, except David and Ezekias and Josias, were defective: for they forsook the law of the most High, even the kings of Juda failed.”

Amaziah did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, “yet not like David his father”, and the high places were not taken away. He is among the defective kings of Judah. Only David, Hezekiah and Josiah are set apart.

points: And of the twelve prophets let the memorial be blessed, and let their bones flourish again out of their place: for they comforted Jacob, and delivered them by assured hope. Let their bones flourish again out of their place. Let them come back again. For they comforted Jacob, and delivered them. The prophets were always sent to deliver the people, because they were created to be saviours.
The remembrance of Josias is like perfume made by the art of the apothecary. The apothecary's oil was consecrated and unlike anything else. If you are not like anything else, you are special.
